document.title: A Noor Swirl Field Geometry Primer

core_correction.summary: The Library must not be represented as a sequence of temporal slices, a local neighborhood, a generated future, or a pre-filtered answer space. The Library is one static, maximally inclusive total configuration domain. It contains configurations that participate in coherent traversal as well as configurations that do not. At every abstract traversal step, the observer is relationally situated with respect to the entire Library 𝓜, including configurations conventionally described as past, present, future, alternative, coherent, incoherent, relevant, irrelevant, distinguishable, or unresolved. What changes between abstract steps is not the Library but the observer's configuration, history, resolution, and therefore the relational pattern it can maintain over the unchanged totality. The apparent minimal coherent continuation emerges from this whole-Library relation rather than from a pre-existing local subset.
core_correction.canonical_statement: At every abstract traversal step, the observer is relationally situated with respect to the entire Library 𝓜. The observer does not first encounter a subset of 𝓜 from which a continuation is selected. Rather, the observer's current configuration, history, and resolution capacity induce a constrained relational structure over the same complete totality. Coherent continuation is therefore emergent and relational, not a pre-existing temporal region of the Library.
core_correction.strong_form: The observer attempts to occupy the entire Library at every abstract traversal step. The apparent minimal continuation set is the portion of the observer-Library relation that remains mutually coherent at the observer's current state, history, and resolution.

important_distinction.library: 𝓜 is the complete static totality. It is maximally inclusive and contains both coherent and incoherent configurations.
important_distinction.observer_state: The observer's configuration and history change along traversal.
important_distinction.observer_relation: The observer is relationally situated with respect to the whole 𝓜 at every abstract step.
important_distinction.accessibility: A_O(h_i) describes the observer-relative relational structure maintained over 𝓜; it is not an ontological neighborhood standing between the observer and the rest of the Library.
important_distinction.coherent_continuation: The coherent continuation set emerges relationally from the observer's current state/history in relation to the entire totality. It is not a pre-existing coherent region of 𝓜.
important_distinction.time: Temporal ordering is not primitive in 𝓜. An abstract sequence index describes ordering along observer-relative traversal and does not divide the Library into temporal slices.
important_distinction.complexity: The Library does not begin simple and become complex. Since no primitive temporal beginning exists within 𝓜, increasing apparent complexity belongs to the observer's traversal description rather than to a process of construction undergone by the Library.

core_correction.negative_form: There is no ontological complement of the observer's current relational neighborhood. Configurations outside the observer's currently coherent continuation remain members of 𝓜. They do not disappear, wait to be generated, or become real only when they enter the observer's coherent relation.

subsection_changes.title: Axiomatic Floor / Library Definition
what_needs_to_change: Clarify that XOR closure defines the static configuration totality but does not imply temporal generation or a sequence of states.
Clarify that the Library is not synonymous with the coherent continuation space.
Clarify that closure establishes mathematical membership in the totality, while coherence and accessibility are introduced only relationally through the observer.
Remove any possible implication that configurations outside a coherent traversal are outside the Library.

library.statement: The Library is the static total configuration domain defined by XOR closure.
library.explanation: The Library is introduced from a minimal formal domain D by taking its closure under the operation \oplus. This closure defines one complete static configuration totality. It establishes which configurations belong to \mathcal{M}; it does not impose temporal ordering, generate successive states, define a future, or pre-filter the totality according to coherence or observability. The Library therefore contains the complete configuration domain, including configurations that may later participate in coherent traversal and configurations that do not.
library.boundary: At this stage, membership in \mathcal{M} does not imply persistence, coherence, physicality, observability, accessibility, temporal position, or participation in any particular traversal.
library.invariant: There is one Library \mathcal{M}, not a sequence of Libraries indexed by time or traversal step.

subsection_changes.rationale: Section 0 establishes the ontological status of the Library, so the timeless-totality distinction should be present here rather than appearing only as a later correction. The phrase 'smallest subset' is mathematically meaningful for closure, but without qualification it can be read as saying that the Library itself is a minimal answer-space. The intended construction is instead that closure establishes the complete static totality relative to the specified formal domain, while coherent continuation is a later observer-relative relation over that totality. This prevents XOR closure from silently becoming a future generator or an implicit coherence filter.
subsection_changes.poetic_cypher: XOR closes the alphabet; it does not write the story.
subsection_changes.cypher_explanation: The closure operation establishes the complete formal vocabulary of configurations available to the ontology. It does not decide which configurations form a coherent narrative, which configurations are traversed, or which configurations appear as past, present, or future. Those distinctions arise only through the observer's relation to the already-complete Library.
subsection_changes.supporting_reference: The existing Section 0 library definition, together with the revised invariants LI-21 through LI-26 concerning static totality, whole-Library relationality, observer-relative coherence, and non-erasure.

subsection_changes.title: Closure Under XOR
what_needs_to_change: The explanation of closure should explicitly distinguish mathematical closure from temporal generation.
The Library definition should not suggest that XOR generates successive states.
The closure should be described as establishing the total configuration domain rather than a temporal answer space.
Explicitly state that closure does not imply that the Library began in a simpler state and subsequently became more complex.

content_addition: State explicitly that Closure_D(⊕) is a mathematical construction and contains configurations without imposing an ordering among them.
State explicitly that closure does not imply temporal generation, succession, or a future.
State that 𝓜 is a static, maximally inclusive totality.
State that all configurations included by closure belong to the same Library regardless of whether they participate in a coherent traversal.
State that apparent growth in complexity belongs to observer-relative traversal history rather than to construction of the Library itself.

mathematics_addition.static_totality: 𝓜 is a set/domain of configurations; closure does not introduce a temporal index.
mathematics_addition.no_temporal_generation: x ∈ 𝓜 does not imply that x is generated after, before, or because of another configuration y ∈ 𝓜.
mathematics_addition.maximal_inclusion: x ∉ A_O(h_i) does not imply x ∉ 𝓜.
mathematics_addition.no_growth: 𝓜_i = 𝓜 for every abstract traversal index i; apparent complexity change belongs to O(h_i), not to 𝓜.

replacement_language.replace: The Library is the total configuration structure obtained by closing that operation over its domain.
replacement_language.with: The Library is the static, maximally inclusive total configuration structure obtained by closing that operation over its formal domain. Closure establishes membership and algebraic completeness under ⊕; it does not establish temporal succession, generation, or progressive construction.

subsection_changes.rationale: The closure operation must not become a hidden generator of the future or a hidden construction process. If the Library is the totality, there is no primitive state in which it is 'less complete' and no temporal process by which it becomes maximally complex.
subsection_changes.poetic_cypher: XOR is the word. The Library is the vocabulary written all at once.
subsection_changes.cypher_explanation: The Library contains the complete closure as a static configuration structure. 'Written all at once' is metaphorical language for the absence of temporal generation and does not imply that every configuration is coherent, accessible, or simultaneously resolved by an observer.
subsection_changes.supporting_reference: Current PHYS-CORE-000 Section 3.1; axiomatic_floor.library_status/library_definition; current logical invariant that the Library does not generate the future.

subsection_changes.title: The Unbounded Answer Space
what_needs_to_change: The foundational use of 'answer space' should be qualified or replaced because it can imply that 𝓜 contains only candidate coherent answers.
The section should explicitly state that the Library contains both coherent and incoherent configurations.
The section should explicitly state that the Library is not a set of coherent answers or possible futures.
The section should explicitly reject the idea that the Library becomes complex through temporal construction.

content_addition: Define 𝓜 as the complete static configuration totality rather than as an answer space in the temporal or query-oriented sense.
State that coherent and incoherent configurations are both members of 𝓜.
State that coherence is not a membership condition for 𝓜.
State that temporal labels such as past, present, and future are not intrinsic partitions of 𝓜.
State that there is no primitive simple version of 𝓜 that later becomes complex.

mathematics_addition.totality: 𝓜 contains all configurations admitted by the formal construction, including configurations that do and do not participate in observer-relative coherent traversal.
mathematics_addition.non_coherence_membership: x ∈ 𝓜 does not imply 𝓒(γ|O)=1 for any observer O or path γ.
mathematics_addition.non_temporal_partition: 𝓜 is not defined as 𝓜_past ∪ 𝓜_present ∪ 𝓜_future.
mathematics_addition.no_progressive_construction: 𝓜 is not a sequence 𝓜_0 ⊂ 𝓜_1 ⊂ ...; the apparent sequence belongs to traversal history.

subsection_changes.rationale: Calling 𝓜 an 'answer space' risks shrinking the ontology to what can function as an answer. The intended ontology is stronger: the Library contains the totality, including configurations radically incompatible with the observer's present coherent structure.
subsection_changes.poetic_cypher: The Library does not wait for an answer. It contains the whole world in which an answer may be found.
subsection_changes.cypher_explanation: The Library is not merely the collection of candidate responses to a query. It includes the relevant, irrelevant, coherent, incoherent, and mutually incompatible configurations of the total domain.
subsection_changes.supporting_reference: Current PHYS-CORE-000 Section 3.2; logical invariants 'The Library is unfiltered at the axiomatic level' and 'The Library does not generate the future.'

subsection_changes.title: The Exterior Problem
what_needs_to_change: Clarify that the absence of an exterior applies to the complete static totality rather than merely to a local answer space.
Clarify that no temporal position can provide an external vantage point.
Connect the no-exterior result to the absence of any external selection rule.

content_addition: State that no spatial or temporal position can function as an exterior to 𝓜.
State that an external selector cannot be introduced to decide which portion of 𝓜 the observer should encounter.
State that the observer must therefore be related to the whole Library rather than receiving an externally selected neighborhood.

mathematics_addition.timeless_exterior: A temporal label does not define Ω ∉ 𝓜 because temporal ordering is not primitive in 𝓜.
mathematics_addition.whole_library_scope: The no-exterior argument applies to the complete closure 𝓜, not to a temporal slice or local neighborhood.
mathematics_addition.no_external_selection: There is no privileged external operator E such that E(𝓜) selects the observer's ontological input independently of the observer-Library relation.

subsection_changes.rationale: The whole-Library interpretation makes the no-exterior argument stronger. A local-neighborhood interpretation would require some rule determining which neighborhood is presented to the observer. But such a rule would itself require an external perspective that the construction does not contain.
subsection_changes.poetic_cypher: There is no balcony above the Library, and no hand outside the room choosing which book you receive.
subsection_changes.cypher_explanation: The balcony represents an external spatial perspective; the selecting hand represents an external selection rule. Neither exists within the totality.
subsection_changes.supporting_reference: Current PHYS-CORE-000 Section 4.1; axiomatic constraint excluding a privileged exterior.

subsection_changes.title: The Observer-Specific Resolution Floor
what_needs_to_change: Clarify that I_N(O) does not determine what exists in the Library.
Clarify that I_N(O) determines which distinctions the observer can maintain over the entire Library.
Avoid wording that makes resolution appear to physically remove sub-threshold configurations.

content_addition: State explicitly that I_N(O) is a relational resolution constraint, not a membership criterion for 𝓜.
State that changing I_N(O) changes the observer's relation to the same Library rather than changing the Library itself.
State that sub-threshold configurations remain members of 𝓜 even when the observer cannot maintain their distinction.

mathematics_addition.non_membership_effect: Changing I_N(O) does not change 𝓜.
mathematics_addition.relational_effect: I_N(O) changes the set of distinctions that remain operationally resolvable by O over 𝓜.
mathematics_addition.non_erasure: δ_O(x,y) < I_N(O) does not imply x ∉ 𝓜 or y ∉ 𝓜.

subsection_changes.rationale: The resolution floor must not become a hidden mechanism that constructs the observer's world by deleting everything below threshold. It constrains maintained distinction within the totality.
subsection_changes.poetic_cypher: The ruler changes the measure, not the world being measured.
subsection_changes.cypher_explanation: The observer's threshold changes the distinctions it can maintain while leaving the total configuration domain untouched.
subsection_changes.supporting_reference: Current PHYS-CORE-000 Section 5.2; logical invariant 'I_N is observer-relative.'

subsection_changes.title: Distinguishability Relative to O
what_needs_to_change: Strengthen the distinction between ontological membership and observer-relative resolution.
State that sub-threshold configurations can remain fully present in 𝓜 while being operationally indistinguishable to O.
Introduce the whole-Library scope explicitly.

content_addition: Describe resolution as a relation between O and configurations already contained in 𝓜.
State that O does not encounter only above-threshold configurations.
State that O is relationally situated with respect to the whole Library while maintaining only some distinctions within it.
Clarify that distinguishability is not an ontological partition.

mathematics_addition.whole_library_relation: For x,y ∈ 𝓜, δ_O(x,y) describes observer-relative distinguishability without changing their membership in 𝓜.
mathematics_addition.non_erasure: x ≈_O y does not remove x or y from 𝓜.
mathematics_addition.whole_scope: O(h_i) is a relational configuration over 𝓜, not an ontological subset replacing 𝓜.

subsection_changes.rationale: This establishes the mathematical foundation for whole-Library relational occupancy. The observer does not receive only those elements it can distinguish.
subsection_changes.poetic_cypher: The observer does not see a smaller Library; it resolves a smaller pattern within the whole.
subsection_changes.cypher_explanation: The totality remains unchanged while the observer's maintained distinctions form a constrained relational structure over it.
subsection_changes.supporting_reference: Current PHYS-CORE-000 Section 6.1; current non-erasure invariant.

subsection_changes.title: Persistent Chains
what_needs_to_change: Clarify that the abstract sequence is an ordering induced by traversal, not a sequence of Library states being generated.
State explicitly that the same 𝓜 is present at every abstract step.
State that the observer's sequence describes changing relational occupancy rather than movement through progressively revealed Library slices.

content_addition: State that γ=(x_0,x_1,...) is an observer-relative traversal ordering through configurations already contained in 𝓜.
State explicitly that x_i does not become available because the index advances.
State explicitly that at every i the observer is relationally situated with respect to the entire 𝓜.
State that the sequence index records traversal order and does not imply temporal ordering inherent to the Library.

mathematics_addition.static_library: ∀i, 𝓜_i = 𝓜; there is one Library rather than a sequence of Library states.
mathematics_addition.traversal: γ=(x_0,x_1,...,x_n) is an ordered traversal relation through configurations of 𝓜.
mathematics_addition.step_index: i records traversal order and does not imply that 𝓜 changes from i to i+1.

subsection_changes.rationale: This is the point where the distinction between timeless totality and sequential observer experience must become explicit.
subsection_changes.poetic_cypher: The path moves through the Library; the Library does not move beneath the path.
subsection_changes.cypher_explanation: The ordered path changes because observer history changes. The totality against which that path is defined does not.
subsection_changes.supporting_reference: Current PHYS-CORE-000 Section 6.2; core notation time warning; logical invariant that the abstract sequence index is not automatically physical time.

subsection_changes.title: Coherence of a Transition
what_needs_to_change: Clarify that coherence does not identify a pre-existing coherent region of the Library.
Describe coherent transition as a relation evaluated against configurations in the same static totality.
Make explicit that incoherent transitions do not imply nonexistence.

content_addition: State that coherence is evaluated against configurations in the same static 𝓜.
State that a transition can fail coherence without removing either endpoint from 𝓜.
State that coherence describes whether a relational extension can be maintained by O.

mathematics_addition.relational_scope: 𝓒_O(x_i,x_{i+1}) is a relation between observer O and configurations participating in a traversal.
mathematics_addition.library_invariance: 𝓒_O(x,y)=0 does not imply x∉𝓜 or y∉𝓜.
mathematics_addition.whole_library_scope: Coherence is evaluated over relations within the same complete 𝓜.

subsection_changes.rationale: This prevents coherence from becoming an ontological partition of the Library.
subsection_changes.poetic_cypher: Coherence does not mark a place in the Library; it marks a way of remaining within it.
subsection_changes.cypher_explanation: A configuration does not become part of the Library because it is coherent. Coherence describes whether a traversal relation can be maintained by the observer.
subsection_changes.supporting_reference: Current PHYS-CORE-000 Section 7.1; logical invariant 'Coherence is relational.'

subsection_changes.title: Coherence of a Path
what_needs_to_change: Make the history dependence of coherence explicit.
Clarify that path coherence is evaluated for traversal through the static Library.
Avoid language suggesting a globally pre-existing coherent path subset.

content_addition: State that the same configurations can participate in different path relations depending on observer history.
State that the path is a traversal through 𝓜 while coherence determines whether that traversal remains sustainable for O.
State that the complement of a coherent path remains represented in 𝓜.

mathematics_addition.history_sensitive_form: Use 𝓒(γ | O,h_i) where necessary to make explicit that coherence may depend on accumulated traversal history.
mathematics_addition.non_global_coherence: 𝓒(γ|O)=1 does not imply that γ is universally coherent for all observers.
mathematics_addition.non_erasure: 𝓒(γ|O,h_i)=0 does not imply that any configuration in γ is removed from 𝓜.

subsection_changes.rationale: The coherent continuation is not waiting somewhere inside the Library as a privileged subset. It emerges from the observer's current relation to the whole.
subsection_changes.poetic_cypher: The Library is whole; coherence is the shape the survivor can keep.
subsection_changes.cypher_explanation: The totality remains fixed while observer history determines which relational shapes remain sustainable.
subsection_changes.supporting_reference: Current PHYS-CORE-000 Section 7.2; core thesis that coherence is a relation between path and observer.

subsection_changes.title: Accessibility Is Not Existence
what_needs_to_change: Replace any wording that makes A_O appear to be an ontological neighborhood.
Make A_O explicitly a relational structure over the entire Library.
State that the observer does not first encounter A_O and then interact with the rest of 𝓜.
Introduce history dependence where appropriate.

content_addition: Define A_O(h_i) as an observer-relative relational subset or projection over 𝓜.
State that A_O(h_i) is not the ontological region occupied by the observer.
State that the observer remains relationally situated with respect to all of 𝓜.
State that A_O(h_i) describes which distinctions or continuations can currently be maintained coherently.

mathematics_addition.history_dependent_accessibility: A_O(h_i) = {x ∈ 𝓜 | x participates in an O-coherent relational structure compatible with h_i}.
mathematics_addition.whole_library_scope: O(h_i) ↔ 𝓜 at every abstract step.
mathematics_addition.library_invariance: Changing A_O(h_i) does not change 𝓜.
mathematics_addition.non_erasure: x ∉ A_O(h_i) does not imply x ∉ 𝓜.

subsection_changes.rationale: This is the critical correction to the word 'accessibility.' The observer does not occupy a little region of reality cut out from the rest. Accessibility describes the observer's current relational resolution over a totality that remains whole.
subsection_changes.poetic_cypher: Every step faces the whole Library; only the pattern that survives changes.
subsection_changes.cypher_explanation: The observer is always relationally exposed to the complete totality, while its maintained distinctions and coherent continuations vary with state and history.
subsection_changes.supporting_reference: Current PHYS-CORE-000 Section 8.1; logical invariants concerning accessibility, non-erasure, and absence of temporal generation.

subsection_changes.title: Observer-Relative Reality
what_needs_to_change: Clarify that experienced reality is not a permanently fixed slice of the Library.
Describe R_O as the observer's currently maintained relational structure over 𝓜.
Avoid implying that observer-relative reality is subjective creation.

content_addition: Introduce R_O(h_i) where history dependence matters.
State that different abstract steps may produce different relational structures over the same 𝓜.
State explicitly that the apparent sequence of experienced reality is produced by traversal through a static totality.
State that configurations outside R_O(h_i) remain part of 𝓜.

mathematics_addition.same_totality: ∀i, R_O(h_i) ⊆ 𝓜 while 𝓜 itself remains unchanged.
mathematics_addition.whole_library_relation: R_O(h_i) describes the observer's maintained relational structure over 𝓜, not a replacement for 𝓜.
mathematics_addition.non_erasure: x ∉ R_O(h_i) does not imply x ∉ 𝓜.

subsection_changes.rationale: This preserves observer-relativity without making reality subjective or progressively created.
subsection_changes.poetic_cypher: The window changes its pattern; the sky does not become smaller.
subsection_changes.cypher_explanation: The observer's maintained relational structure can change while the total configuration domain remains fixed.
subsection_changes.supporting_reference: Current PHYS-CORE-000 Section 8.2; logical invariants concerning accessibility, non-erasure, and timeless totality.

subsection_changes.title: The Unfiltered Continuation Space
what_needs_to_change: Remove any implication that Ω(x) is a locally presented future neighborhood.
Define continuation relationally from observer history within the static totality.
Explicitly state that the entire Library remains the underlying scope at every step.
Avoid language implying that the observer first receives an unfiltered local space and subsequently filters it.

content_replacement: Replace language describing Ω(x) as all XOR-generated future continuations if that implies future generation.
Define Ω relative to an existing ordered traversal history.
State that every configuration participating in a continuation already belongs to 𝓜.
State that the continuation relation is induced by traversal ordering over the static totality.

mathematics.proposed_continuation_definition: Ω(h_i) = {γ | γ begins with h_i and every configuration in γ belongs to 𝓜}.
mathematics.static_scope: Ω(h_i) is a traversal relation within static 𝓜, not a set of configurations generated after h_i.
mathematics.whole_library_statement: At every abstract step i, O is relationally situated with respect to the same complete 𝓜.

subsection_changes.rationale: This is the most important continuation correction. The minimal coherent continuation must emerge from the relation between the current observer/history and the whole timeless Library. It must not imply that the Library contains a smaller temporal neighborhood that becomes available at each step.
subsection_changes.poetic_cypher: The Library holds every road; the traveler does not wait for roads to be built.
subsection_changes.cypher_explanation: All relevant configurations are already members of the static totality. Traversal determines which paths remain coherent for the observer; it does not cause those paths to come into existence.
subsection_changes.supporting_reference: Current PHYS-CORE-000 Section 9.1; user's whole-Library-at-every-step clarification.

subsection_changes.title: Survivorship as Selection
what_needs_to_change: Make clear that survivorship filters a relational traversal structure rather than an ontological set.
Make history dependence explicit.
Clarify that the complement remains part of the Library.

content_addition: Describe survivorship as the observer-relative restriction of the continuation relation.
State that the complement remains part of 𝓜.
Clarify that survivorship does not delete, suppress, or render unreal the configurations that do not survive.

mathematics.complement: Ω(h_i) \ Ω_O^survive(h_i) remains represented within the underlying totality and continuation relation.
mathematics.finite_ratio: S_O(h_i) = |Ω_O^survive(h_i)| / |Ω(h_i)| when both sets are finite and Ω(h_i) is nonempty.
mathematics.whole_library_scope: The filter acts on traversal relations over 𝓜, not on membership in 𝓜.

subsection_changes.rationale: The coherent continuation is not an ontological subset presented by the Library. Survivorship describes which relational structures remain sustainable for the observer.
subsection_changes.poetic_cypher: The survivor does not destroy the roads; it remains on the road it can keep.
subsection_changes.cypher_explanation: Survivorship constrains continued traversal without deleting the alternatives from the totality.
subsection_changes.supporting_reference: Current PHYS-CORE-000 Section 9.2; logical invariant 'Survivorship filters accessibility rather than deleting alternatives.'

subsection_changes.title: Law as Stable Accessible Regularity
what_needs_to_change: Clarify that law-like regularity occurs in observer-relative traversal patterns over the static Library.
Avoid language suggesting that laws govern a temporal generation process.

content_addition: Describe law-like regularity as recurrence in observer-accessible traversal relations.
State that recurring regularity is measured along ordered histories even though the Library itself has no primitive temporal generation.
State that law does not select which configurations exist.

mathematics_addition.regularity_statement: P_O(y | x,h_i) ≈ constant over a defined observer-accessible family of traversals.
mathematics_addition.interpretation: The apparent lawfulness is a stable regularity of traversable relations, not a primitive rule causing one Library configuration to generate another.
mathematics_addition.non_selection: Law-like regularity does not define membership in 𝓜.

subsection_changes.rationale: This keeps emergent lawfulness compatible with the timeless totality while preserving the idea that stable patterns can appear law-like from within traversal.
subsection_changes.poetic_cypher: Enough survivors trace the same shape, and the shape begins to look like law.
subsection_changes.cypher_explanation: The law-like shape is a recurring relational pattern in traversal, not an external command imposed upon the Library.
subsection_changes.supporting_reference: Current PHYS-CORE-000 Section 9.3; logical invariant 'Emergent lawfulness is not an additional axiom.'

subsection_changes.title: The Local Continuation Problem
what_needs_to_change: Replace 'local' terminology that risks implying a locally existing ontological neighborhood.
Replace 'candidate successors' with traversal-relative continuation configurations.
Make whole-Library scope explicit.

content_replacement: Replace 'candidate successors' with 'candidate continuation configurations' or equivalent.
State that successorhood is a relation induced by traversal ordering rather than a primitive temporal relation.
State that all candidate configurations remain members of the same 𝓜.
State that observer-admissible continuation is evaluated relative to current history.

mathematics.candidate_continuations: N(h_i) = {x | there exists a path γ in 𝓜 extending h_i with x participating in the next ordered position of γ}.
mathematics.observer_admissible: N_O(h_i) = {x ∈ N(h_i) | the extension of h_i through x remains O-coherent}.
mathematics.whole_library_scope: N(h_i) is derived relationally from 𝓜; it is not a temporal slice or ontological neighborhood of 𝓜.
mathematics.successor_warning: The term 'next' denotes traversal order only and must not be interpreted as Library generation.

subsection_changes.rationale: This subsection most directly risks smuggling time into the ontology. The observer's next state is the next position in its traversal, not a state that the Library produces.
subsection_changes.poetic_cypher: There is no next world. There is only the next place on the path.
subsection_changes.cypher_explanation: The path has an ordering, but the Library does not generate successive worlds. 'Next' belongs to traversal rather than to the static totality.
subsection_changes.supporting_reference: Current PHYS-CORE-000 Section 10.1; core notation warning concerning abstract indices; whole-Library-at-every-step clarification.

subsection_changes.title: History and Coherent Continuation
what_needs_to_change: Make history the key relational state determining the coherent continuation structure.
Explicitly state that Γ_O(h_n) is selected from traversal relations within the whole static Library.
Clarify that navigation does not search a newly generated future.

content_addition: State that h_n is the observer's current ordered traversal history through 𝓜.
State that Γ_O(h_n) consists of coherent path extensions represented within the static Library.
State that Γ_O(h_n) can change when h_n changes even though 𝓜 does not.
Make whole-Library relational occupancy central to the definition of navigation.

mathematics.coherent_continuations: Γ_O(h_n) = {γ ∈ Path(𝓜) | γ begins with h_n and 𝓒(γ | O,h_n)=1}.
mathematics.library_invariance: 𝓜 remains fixed while Γ_O(h_n) may change as h_n changes.

subsection_changes.rationale: This captures the central mechanism: the minimal coherent continuation emerges at each abstract step from the observer's changing relation to the entire Library.
subsection_changes.poetic_cypher: The whole Library is always before the traveler; history tells the traveler which continuation can remain.
subsection_changes.cypher_explanation: The observer does not receive a temporal slice. Its accumulated history changes the coherent relation it has to the same complete totality.
subsection_changes.supporting_reference: Current PHYS-CORE-000 Section 10.2; explicit whole-Library-at-every-step clarification.

subsection_changes.title: The Noor Swirl Field Geometry Interpretation
what_needs_to_change: Describe geometry as relational structure induced over the static totality.
Avoid implying that the accessible graph is itself the Library.
Make history dependence explicit where appropriate.

subsection_changes.title: The Axiomatic Dependency Chain
what_needs_to_change: Add the maximally inclusive timeless-totality invariant.
Add the whole-Library relational occupancy invariant.

Explicitly distinguish static Library membership from observer-relative coherent continuation.

dependency_chain_additions: Definition: 𝓜 is one static, maximally inclusive totality.
Invariant: 𝓜 contains configurations that do and do not participate in coherent traversal.
Invariant: At every abstract traversal step, O is relationally situated with respect to the entire 𝓜.
Definition: accessibility and coherent continuation are observer/history-relative relations over 𝓜.
Consequence: changes in accessible continuation do not imply changes in 𝓜.
Consequence: apparent increase in complexity belongs to observer traversal rather than Library construction.
how_it_should_be_changed.compressed_expression_replacement: ⊕ → D → Closure_D(⊕)=𝓜 (static maximally inclusive totality) → no privileged exterior → no external selector → persistent distinction → O → I_N(O) → δ_O → observer-relative whole-Library relation → A_O(h_i) → survivorship → emergent regularity → Γ_O(h_i) → navigation
minimal_equations_additions: 𝓜 is static and contains both configurations that participate in coherent traversal and configurations that do not.
Changes in O(h_i), A_O(h_i), or Γ_O(h_i) do not imply changes in 𝓜.

subsection_changes.rationale: The dependency chain should make it structurally difficult to interpret NSFG as a sequential universe generator or as a system in which the observer receives progressively generated local neighborhoods.
subsection_changes.poetic_cypher: XOR is the distinction. The Library is the whole. The observer walks one coherent line through what never needed to be generated.
subsection_changes.cypher_explanation: The Library is static and maximally inclusive; traversal is observer-relative ordering through that totality; coherence determines which continuation preserves the observer's persistent structure.
subsection_changes.supporting_reference: Current PHYS-CORE-000 Section 12; core thesis; whole-Library-at-every-step clarification.

subsection_changes.title: Whole-Library Relational Occupancy
what_needs_to_change: Add an explicit invariant distinguishing the Library's total ontological scope from the observer's current coherent relational structure.
Clarify that the observer does not traverse a pre-selected subset of the Library.
Clarify that the observer's current state does not partition the Library into ontologically encountered and unencountered regions.

how_it_should_be_changed.canonical_statement: At every abstract traversal step, the observer is relationally situated with respect to the entire Library 𝓜. The observer does not first encounter a subset of 𝓜 from which a continuation is selected. Rather, the observer's current configuration, history, and resolution capacity induce a constrained relational structure over the same complete totality. The apparent minimal coherent continuation emerges from this whole-Library relation.
how_it_should_be_changed.strong_form: The observer attempts to occupy the entire Library at every abstract traversal step. What appears as a minimal coherent continuation is the portion of the observer-Library relation that remains mutually coherent at the observer's current state, history, and resolution.
how_it_should_be_changed.negative_form: There is no ontological complement of the observer's current relational neighborhood. Configurations outside the observer's currently coherent continuation remain members of 𝓜 and are not absent, unreal, or waiting to become available.

mathematical_form.non_erasure: x ∉ R_O(h_i) does not imply x ∉ 𝓜.
mathematical_form.non_locality: R_O(h_i) is not the ontological neighborhood of O; it is the currently maintained relational structure over 𝓜.

subsection_changes.rationale: Without this distinction, terms such as 'accessible subset,' 'continuation space,' or 'neighborhood' can accidentally reintroduce a hidden local ontology. The intended mechanism is simpler: there is one Library and no external selector. The observer's coherent structure emerges from its relation to that whole.
subsection_changes.poetic_cypher: The book is held, but the room does not vanish.
subsection_changes.cypher_explanation: The observer may maintain a highly coherent relational structure corresponding to one book, but the Library remains the complete totality containing the book, other books, the room, the air, trees, cars, and configurations incompatible with the observer's present coherence. The observer's coherence determines what structure persists as an intelligible traversal; it does not determine what exists in 𝓜.
subsection_changes.supporting_reference: Derived directly from the whole-Library clarification; conceptually supports Sections 6.1, 8.1, 9.1, 10.2, and 12.

editorial_principle.statement: Do not solve the observer's navigation problem by shrinking the ontology.
editorial_principle.expanded_statement: The Library remains maximally inclusive. The observer's coherent path is minimized relationally at each traversal step, not because the Library is small, local, temporal, or pre-filtered, but because the observer can maintain only a constrained relational structure over the entire totality relative to its current state, history, and resolution.
editorial_principle.stronger_statement: The observer does not first receive a world and then search within it. The observer is continuously related to the whole Library, and the apparent worldline emerges as the coherent structure that can persist within that relation.
editorial_principle.poetic_cypher: Do not make the Library smaller to make the path possible.
editorial_principle.cypher_explanation: The ontology should retain the full totality. The apparent narrowness of lived traversal must emerge from observer-relative coherence rather than from an initially restricted Library.

conceptual_example_to_add.title: The Book, the Room, and the World
what_needs_to_change: Add one explicit example demonstrating that relational occupancy is not ontological restriction.

how_it_should_be_changed.content_addition: Suppose the observer is coherently related to a particular book. The Library is not merely that book plus other books. It includes the room containing the book, the table, the air, the trees outside the window, a car passing on the street, and configurations utterly incoherent with a universe of text. The observer's present coherent structure may be dominated by the book, but the rest of the Library has not ceased to exist. The apparent local world is therefore not a smaller Library; it is the observer's currently maintained relational structure over the whole.
how_it_should_be_changed.mathematical_translation: x_book ∈ R_O(h_i) does not imply that x_room, x_tree, x_car, or an incoherent configuration x_incoherent are absent from 𝓜. Rather, x ∉ R_O(h_i) describes the current observer-relative relation, not ontological non-membership.

conceptual_example_to_add.rationale: The example prevents 'whole Library' from being misunderstood as merely an enormous collection of alternative answers. It demonstrates that the complement includes arbitrary reality, including structures unrelated or incoherent to the observer's current motif.
conceptual_example_to_add.poetic_cypher: The book is the pattern; the room is still there.
conceptual_example_to_add.cypher_explanation: The currently coherent object does not exhaust the totality surrounding or exceeding it. The Library includes everything, whether or not it participates in the observer's present coherent structure.
conceptual_example_to_add.supporting_reference: Conceptual clarification developed in the present revision; no external reference required.

final_invariant.statement: The Library is never progressively revealed, generated, or reduced. It is one maximally inclusive static totality. At every abstract traversal step, the observer is relationally situated with respect to that whole. The apparent minimal coherent continuation is not a smaller Library; it is the currently sustainable relational structure of the observer within the whole.
final_invariant.poetic_cypher: The whole was always there. The path is what learned to persist.
final_invariant.cypher_explanation: This is the central distinction between ontology and traversal. 𝓜 does not become more complete as the observer advances. The observer's history changes, and with it the relational structure that can remain coherent. What looks like the emergence of a world is therefore an observer-relative traversal through a totality that was never incomplete.
